name: Haiku · 5–7–5 practice
origin: English-language teaching adaptation of Japanese haiku
summary: A three-line syllabic exercise: five, seven, five. Capture a moment with precise, concrete images.
notes: Japanese on (morae) are not equivalent to English syllables. This is an explicitly labeled English practice variant.
Contemporary English-language haiku need not follow 5–7–5. Seasonal context and a cut or juxtaposition also matter.

sources.title: The Haiku Foundation — Line and syllable count
